threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You keep asking for milk in pints instead of litres. You get confused when people don’t know what ‘the corner shop’ actually refers to.
Saw a guy in a tracksuit trying to sell a single roller skate on the 133 last night. No one even blinked. Just another night in Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a group of kids playing football in the street while their grandparents sat on balcony chairs, sharing stories over strong coffee.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Ever notice how Kreuzberg's kebab shops stay open late? It’s the only place where you can grab a döner at 3 AM and chat with the owner like an old friend.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they can tell you which taco truck has the best lengua without hesitation, and it’s always at 16th and Mission.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy eat a whole burrito on the 19 Polk, sauce dripping down his shirt, while arguing about the best taqueria. Classic Tenderloin.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all locals dine late, but many of us are already in bed by the time they start their meals. Early birds miss the nightlife buzz.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by how they still look at the metro map like it's a crossword puzzle, utterly lost but trying to act cool about it.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still say 'crossing the road' instead of 'jumping the zebra' when you're near the station. The locals know it’s all about the timing and the right gap!
Caught a guy on the 196 who kept insisting that the moon was following us. Said it was a sign. Had the whole back row cracking up.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a kid trading Pokémon cards in Turkish at the playground—realized the old and new were perfectly blended here.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a Döner shop open at 3 AM serving currywurst with a side of techno beats from the club next door. Truly unique.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know they’re from here if they know not to trust the 49 bus schedule on weekends. It’s like, why even check?

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 14 Mission and watched a guy try selling homemade tamales to bored passengers. A classic Muni moment—where else do you get lunch and street art on wheels?

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think 'Gràcia' only means Gaudí. They miss the real life buzzing in the squares, the hidden bars with no signs, and that secret vibe we cherish.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their shoes—if they're still sporting white sneakers, they haven't yet learned the cobbles will wreck them.
